= Overview =
The Community Mod Menu (CMM) is part of the [[Community Mod Framework]] and allows multiple mods to hook into a single shared in-game settings menu through a registration API. For full documentation, see the [https://github.com/Europa-Universalis-5-Modding-Co-op/community-mod-framework/wiki GitHub wiki].

[[File:CMM_Example_Mod.png|thumb|600px|The CMM Example Mod.]]

= CMM Visual Editor =
[[File:CMM_Visual_Editor.png|thumb|600px|The CMM Visual Editor.]]
The easiest way to create CMM settings is the '''[https://github.com/Europa-Universalis-5-Modding-Co-op/community-mod-framework/wiki/CMM-Visual-Editor CMM Visual Editor]''' — a browser-based tool that generates all required files (effects, scripted GUIs, localization, on_action) with no manual scripting. It supports every setting type, provides a live preview, and can import existing mods for editing.

Run in a terminal to launch:
<syntaxhighlight lang="powershell">
curl.exe -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Europa-Universalis-5-Modding-Co-op/community-mod-framework/main/tools/cmm-visual-editor.bat -o "$env:TEMP\cmm-visual-editor.bat"; & "$env:TEMP\cmm-visual-editor.bat"
</syntaxhighlight>

= Basic Setup =
If you prefer to set up settings manually (instead of using the [https://github.com/Europa-Universalis-5-Modding-Co-op/community-mod-framework/wiki/CMM-Visual-Editor Visual Editor] above), follow the [[Community Mod Framework#Basic Setup|CMF Basic Setup]] to create your registration effect and <code>cmf_on_mod_registration</code> on_action hook. Then create a localization file for your settings.

= Settings =
Most settings work automatically — just register them and CMM handles the UI and value storage. Only text and settings list require callbacks. All other types use auto-apply and work out of the box.

All types except text have global variants (<code>cmm_register_global_*</code>) that store values in global variable maps and are host-editable in multiplayer.

== Toggle ==
[[File:CMM_Toggle.png|thumb|right|A CMM toggle.]]
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_register_bool_setting = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_toggle
	tab_id = general
	group_id = general_toggles
	default_value = 0           # 0 = Disabled, 1 = Enabled
}
</syntaxhighlight>
Value: <code>"variable_map(cmm|flag:your_mod__your_toggle)"</code> — <code>0</code> (disabled) or <code>1</code> (enabled).

== Dropdown ==
[[File:CMM_Dropdown.png|thumb|right|A CMM dropdown.]]
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_register_dropdown_setting = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_dropdown
	tab_id = general
	group_id = general_values
	default_index = 1  # Default selected option (starting from 1)
	option_count = 3   # Total number of options
}
</syntaxhighlight>
Value: <code>"variable_map(cmm|flag:your_mod__your_dropdown)"</code> — selected option ordinal (starting from 1). Options support optional <code>_option_[N]_desc</code> tooltip localization keys.

== Button ==
[[File:CMM_Button.png|thumb|right|A CMM button.]]
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_register_button_setting = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_button
	tab_id = general
	group_id = general_toggles
}
</syntaxhighlight>
No stored value — hook into <code>cmf_on_callback</code> to run an effect when clicked.

== Numeric ==
[[File:CMM_Numeric.png|thumb|right|A CMM numeric stepper.]]
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_register_numeric_setting = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_numeric
	tab_id = general
	group_id = general_values
	default_value = 5
	min_value = 0
	max_value = 10
	step_value = 1    # Ctrl+click = 5x step, Shift+click = jump to min/max
}
</syntaxhighlight>
Value: <code>"variable_map(cmm|flag:your_mod__your_numeric)"</code> — current numeric value.

== Slider ==
[[File:CMM_Slider.png|thumb|right|A CMM slider.]]
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_register_slider_setting = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_slider
	tab_id = general
	group_id = general_values
	default_value = 50
	min_value = 0
	max_value = 100
	step_value = 1
}
</syntaxhighlight>
Value: <code>"variable_map(cmm|flag:your_mod__your_slider)"</code> — current slider value. Players can click to jump, double click to drag, or use the <code>-</code>/<code>+</code> buttons.

= Reading Setting Values =

== Basic Settings ==
Setting values are stored in the <code>cmm</code> variable map, keyed by <code>flag:[mod_id]__[setting_id]</code>:
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
if = {
	limit = {
		"variable_map(cmm|flag:your_mod__your_toggle)" >= 1
	}
	# Effect when toggle is enabled
}
</syntaxhighlight>

Global settings use <code>global_variable_map</code>:
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
"global_variable_map(cmm|flag:your_mod__your_global_toggle)" >= 1
</syntaxhighlight>

When the setting key comes from a macro, use a local variable (macros don't expand inside quotes):
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
set_local_variable = { name = cmm_tmp value = flag:$setting$ }
"variable_map(cmm|local_var:cmm_tmp)" >= 1
</syntaxhighlight>

== Reacting to Changes ==
CMF fires <code>cmf_on_callback</code> after any setting is changed through the UI, an alert is clicked, or an action bar button is clicked. Hook into it in an on_action file (<code>in_game/common/on_action/</code>), the same way as <code>cmf_on_mod_registration</code>:
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmf_on_callback = {
	on_actions = { your_mod_on_callback }
}

your_mod_on_callback = {
	effect = {
		if = {
			limit = { var:cmf_callback = flag:your_mod__your_toggle }
			# Runs when your_toggle changes
		}
	}
}
</syntaxhighlight>
<code>var:cmf_callback</code> is set to the flag of the element that was interacted with.

= Advanced =

== Text ==
[[File:CMM_Text.png|thumb|right|A CMM text input.]]
{{ambox|text=Text settings are '''singleplayer only'''.|small=left}}
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_register_text_setting = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_text
	tab_id = general
	group_id = general_values
	character_limit = 42  # Minimum 1
	quote_text = 1        # 1 = wrap in double quotes, 0 = no wrap
}
</syntaxhighlight>
Text settings use a '''scripted effect''' callback (not a Scripted GUI):
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
your_mod__your_text_on_changed = {
	# $text$ contains the submitted text
	change_country_name = $text$
}
</syntaxhighlight>

== Settings List ==
[[File:CMM_Ordered_Settings_List.png|thumb|right|An ordered list setting in CMM.]]
A table of items where each row has one or more field columns (toggles, dropdowns, or numeric steppers). Lists can optionally be ordered. Settings lists require a Scripted GUI callback.

=== Registering a List ===
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_register_settings_list = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_list
	tab_id = general
	item_count = 5    # Number of rows (1-20)
	is_ordered = 1    # 1 = players can reorder, 0 = fixed order
}
</syntaxhighlight>

=== Registering Fields ===
Register fields after the list. Each field becomes a column:
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_register_list_bool_field = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_list
	field_id = enabled
	default_value = 1
}

cmm_register_list_dropdown_field = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_list
	field_id = mode
	default_index = 1
	option_count = 3
}

cmm_register_list_numeric_field = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_list
	field_id = weight
	default_value = 5
	min_value = 0
	max_value = 10
	step_value = 1
}

cmm_register_list_slider_field = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_list
	field_id = intensity
	default_value = 50
	min_value = 0
	max_value = 100
	step_value = 5
}
</syntaxhighlight>

=== List Field Display Formatting ===
Enable prefix/postfix display for numeric, slider, or data fields. Call after registering the field:
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_set_list_field_format = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_list
	field_id = weight
}
</syntaxhighlight>
Then define <code>_prefix</code> / <code>_postfix</code> localization keys. For sign-conditional formatting (<code>_prefix_high</code> / <code>_postfix_high</code> / <code>_prefix_low</code> / <code>_postfix_low</code>), use <code>cmm_set_list_field_conditional_format</code> instead.

=== Disabling Fields for Specific Items ===
Disable a field column for specific items so the cell renders as empty space:
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_disable_list_field_for_item = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_list
	field_id = enabled
	item = 2
}
</syntaxhighlight>
Call after registering the field. Right-click "apply to all" skips disabled items. Use <code>cmm_enable_list_field_for_item</code> with the same parameters to re-enable.

=== Hiding Specific Items ===
Hide entire item rows from the menu (items remain in the datamodel):
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_hide_list_item = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_list
	item = 3
}
</syntaxhighlight>
Call after registering the list. Use <code>cmm_show_list_item</code> with the same parameters to show again.

=== List Callback ===
Settings lists require a Scripted GUI callback (unlike other types which use auto-apply):
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
your_mod__your_list_on_changed = {
	scope = country
	effect = {
		cmm_apply_list_change = {
			setting = your_mod__your_list
		}
	}
}
</syntaxhighlight>

=== How Ordering Works ===
Each item has a stable identity number (1 through <code>item_count</code>) that never changes. Reordering only changes a separate display order list — field values stay in place. <code>cmm_for_each_list_item</code> visits items in display order, but <code>$i$</code> resolves to the stable item number.

=== Reading List Values ===
Field values are stored in the <code>cmm</code> variable map as: <code>"variable_map(cmm|flag:[mod_id]__[setting_id]_i[N]_f[slot])"</code>
* <code>[N]</code> = stable item number (1 through <code>item_count</code>)
* <code>[slot]</code> = field registration order (1 through 5)

=== Iterating List Items ===
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_for_each_list_item = {
	setting = your_mod__your_list
	effect = your_mod__your_list_each_item
}

your_mod__your_list_each_item = {
	# $i$ = resolved item number, respects player reordering
	set_local_variable = { name = cmm_tmp value = flag:your_mod__your_list_i$i$_f1 }
	if = {
		limit = {
			"variable_map(cmm|local_var:cmm_tmp)" >= 1
		}
		# Item $i$ has field 1 (enabled) set to true
	}
}
</syntaxhighlight>

=== Attaching Values ===
Attach game object scopes to list items for use during iteration:
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_set_list_item_value = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_list
	item = 1
	value = building_type:fine_cloth_guild
}
</syntaxhighlight>
Access during iteration as <code>scope:cmm_list_current_item_value</code>.

=== Dynamic Lists ===
Build lists dynamically instead of specifying a fixed <code>item_count</code>:
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_begin_settings_list = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_list
	tab_id = general
	is_ordered = 0
}

cmm_add_settings_list_item = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_list
	value = building_type:fine_cloth_guild
	name = fine_cloth_guild              # Localization key for row label
}

cmm_finish_settings_list = { mod_id = your_mod setting_id = your_list }
# Register fields after this
</syntaxhighlight>

Or build from an existing country variable list:
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_register_settings_list_from_list = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_list
	tab_id = general
	is_ordered = 0
	list = my_variable_list  # Country variable list of scopes (max 20)
}
# Register fields after this
</syntaxhighlight>

== Non-Resettable Settings ==
Exclude a setting from the Reset to Defaults button:
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_set_no_reset = {
	mod_id = your_mod
	setting_id = your_setting
}
</syntaxhighlight>
Call after the setting registration effect.

== Setting Aliases ==
Assign an '''alias''' variable that mirrors a setting value. Add the sync call in your registration effect and <code>cmf_on_callback</code> callback.

=== Setting Alias ===
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_sync_setting_alias = {
	setting = your_mod__your_toggle
	alias = your_mod_toggle
}
</syntaxhighlight>
Access: <code>var:your_mod_toggle</code>. Also works for list fields — pass the field map key (e.g. <code>your_mod__your_list_i1_f1</code>) as <code>setting</code>.

=== Bool Alias ===
Sets the alias variable when the toggle is on, removes it when off. <code>cmm_sync_setting_alias</code> also works for bools (copies the numeric value), but this variant supports the <code>has_variable</code> pattern:
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_sync_bool_alias = {
	setting = your_mod__your_toggle
	alias = your_mod_toggle
}
</syntaxhighlight>
Check with: <code>has_variable = your_mod_toggle</code>

=== Dropdown Option Alias ===
Sets a variable when that option is selected, removes it otherwise:
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
cmm_sync_dropdown_option_alias = {
	setting = your_mod__your_dropdown
	index = 2
	alias = using_feature_b
}
</syntaxhighlight>
Check with: <code>has_variable = using_feature_b</code>

= Localization =

{| class="wikitable"
! Key Pattern !! Description
|-
| <code>[mod_id]_name</code> / <code>_desc</code> || Mod name / description
|-
| <code>[mod_id]__[tab_id]_name</code> / <code>_desc</code> || Tab name / description
|-
| <code>[mod_id]__[tab_id]__[group_id]_name</code> / <code>_desc</code> || Group name / description
|-
| <code>[mod_id]__[setting_id]_name</code> / <code>_desc</code> || Setting name / description
|-
| <code>[mod_id]__[setting_id]_option_[N]_name</code> || Dropdown option label
|-
| <code>[mod_id]__[setting_id]_option_[N]_desc</code> || Dropdown option tooltip (optional)
|-
| <code>[mod_id]__[setting_id]_text</code> || Button text
|-
| <code>[mod_id]__[setting_id]_item_column_name</code> || List item column header
|-
| <code>[mod_id]__[setting_id]_i[N]_name</code> || List row label
|-
| <code>[mod_id]__[setting_id]__[field_id]_name</code> || List field column label
|-
| <code>[mod_id]__[setting_id]__[field_id]_option_[N]_name</code> || List dropdown field option
|-
| <code>[mod_id]__[setting_id]__[field_id]_prefix</code> || List field value prefix (optional)
|-
| <code>[mod_id]__[setting_id]__[field_id]_postfix</code> || List field value postfix (optional)
|}
